MAN.About: Naabu is a high-speed, lightweight cybersecurity tool used to scan networks and identify open ports

Port Options.-port or -p: Ports to scan (single port or range)
Port Options.-top-ports or -tp: Number of top ports to scan
Port Options.-exclude-ports or -ep: Ports to exclude from scan , seperated
Port Options.-ports-file or -pf: Ports to scan from a file
Port Options.-exclude-cdn or -ec: skip full port scans for CDN's

Configuration Options.-scan-all-ips or -sa: scan all the IP's associated with DNS record
Configuration Options.-source-ip: source ip (It is used to manually specify a ip and port for outgoing scan)
Configuration Options.-interface or -i: network Interface to use for port scan
Configuration Options.-nmap-cli: nmap command to run on found results (example: -nmap-cli 'nmap -sV')
Configuration Options.-r: list of custom resolver dns resolution , separated
Configuration Options.-stream: stream mode (disables resume, nmap, verify, retries, shuffling, etc)

Miscellaneous.-stats: display stats of the running scan
Miscellaneous.-si or -stats-interval: int number of seconds to wait between showing a statistics update (default 5)

MAN.About: Subfinder is a passive subdomain discovery tool,Subfinder can be used to obtain a number of valid subdomains both passively and actively, to identify more attack surface

INPUT.-d or -domain [string]: Specific target domains to find subdomains for
INPUT.-dL or -list [string]: string: Path to a text file containing a list of target domains for batch discovery

SOURCE.-s or -source [string]: Specific passive sources/services to use for enumeration (e.g., -s crtsh,github).
SOURCE.-recursive: Natively use only passive sources that support recursive subdomain discovery
SOURCE.-all: Query every available passive source for enumeration (maximizes coverage but is slower)
SOURCE.-es or -exclude-sources [string]: string[]: Specific passive sources to completely omit from the search

FILTER.-m or -match [string]: Subdomain string or path to a file with subdomains to explicitly match
FILTER.-f or -filter [string]: Subdomain string or path to a file with subdomains to filter out
FILTER.-match-regex [string]: A regex expression or path to a file containing regex to match on output subdomains
FILTER.-filter-regex [string]: string[]: A regex expression or path to a file containing regex to filter out from output subdomains

RATE LIMIT.-rl or -rate-limit [int]: Maximum number of global HTTP requests allowed to send per second
RATE LIMIT.-rls or -rate-limits [value]: Custom per-provider rate limits (e.g., separating limits for different APIs)
RATE LIMIT.-t [int]: Number of concurrent goroutines used specifically for resolving subdomains (defaults to 10, works with -active only)

CONFIGURATION.-config [string]: string: Path to a custom Subfinder flag configuration file (defaults to $HOME/.config/subfinder/config.yaml)
CONFIGURATION.-pc or -provider-config [string]: Path to the API provider settings configuration file (defaults to $HOME/.config/subfinder/provider-config.yaml)
CONFIGURATION.-r [string]: Comma-separated list of custom DNS resolvers to use.
CONFIGURATION.-rL or -rlist [string]: Path to a file containing a list of custom DNS resolvers
CONFIGURATION.-nW or -active: Forces the tool to validate and display active/live subdomains only
CONFIGURATION.-proxy [string]: The HTTP proxy string to tunnel Subfinder's traffic through.
CONFIGURATION.-ei or -exclude-ip: : Excludes resolved IP addresses from the final domains list output

DEBUG.-silent: Supresses all banners and operational metadata, displaying only found subdomains in the stdout
DEBUG.-version: Displays the active version details of Subfinder.
DEBUG.-v: Enables verbose output to log real-time scanning errors, warnings, and current operations

UPDATE.-up or -update: Automatically updates the Subfinder engine binary to the latest release version available
UPDATE.-duc or -disable-update-check: Prevents Subfinder from checking for new version releases automatically on launch

MAN.About: Amass is a network mapping and attack surface discovery tool used for discovering domains, subdomains, IP addresses, and related infrastructure.

Target Input & Scoping.-d: Target root domain name. Can be specified multiple times for bulk operations.
Target Input & Scoping.-df: Path to a text file containing a list of target root domains.
Target Input & Scoping.-asn: Limits or targets discovery to specific Autonomous System Numbers.
Target Input & Scoping.-cidr: Limits or targets discovery to specific CIDR IP blocks.
Target Input & Scoping.-addr: Comma-separated list of exact IP addresses or ranges to parse (intel only).
Target Input & Scoping.-bl: Specific subdomain names to exclude from processing.
Target Input & Scoping.-blf: Path to a file containing line-separated blacklisted subdomains.
Target Input & Scoping.-nf: Path to a file containing known subdomain names harvested from other tools.

Reconnaissance & Mode Modifiers.-passive: Prevents active validation and relies strictly on OSINT data feeds.
Reconnaissance & Mode Modifiers.-active: Touches target infrastructure directly through active DNS validation, zone transfers, or target SSL/TLS certificates.
Reconnaissance & Mode Modifiers.-whois: Forces WHOIS lookup correlation to uncover associated asset domains managed by the same entities (intel only).

Brute-Forcing & Name Alterations.-w: Custom path to an external subdomain wordlist file.
Brute-Forcing & Name Alterations.-norecursive: Stops further recursive brute-forcing workflows on discovered sub-elements.
Brute-Forcing & Name Alterations.-min-for-recursive: Minimum number of confirmed subdomain levels before deeper recursion triggers (default: 1).
Brute-Forcing & Name Alterations.-noalts: Disables generation of mutated or altered word variations of discovered names.
Brute-Forcing & Name Alterations.-aw: Custom dictionary path used to generate name mutations and alterations.
Brute-Forcing & Name Alterations.-wm: Custom formatting mask rules for name mutations.

Integrations & Data Source Filters.-list: Lists all available passive data sources and APIs compiled into the engine.
Integrations & Data Source Filters.-include: Comma-separated strict inclusion list of data source providers.
Integrations & Data Source Filters.-if: Path to a file identifying data sources to strictly include.
Integrations & Data Source Filters.-exclude: Comma-separated list of data sources to disregard.
Integrations & Data Source Filters.-ef: Path to a file defining data sources to exclude from execution profiles.

Display & Data Export Formats.-o: Path to an output text file where discovered domains are recorded.
Display & Data Export Formats.-oA: Prefix used to generate output files in all supported operational formats simultaneously (.txt, .json, .graph).
Display & Data Export Formats.-json: Exports findings as structured JSON lines to the designated file path.
Display & Data Export Formats.-src: Includes the origin source service in each output entry.
Display & Data Export Formats.-ip: Appends verified IPv4 and IPv6 addresses to findings.
Display & Data Export Formats.-ipv4: Restricts IP logging output to IPv4 addresses.
Display & Data Export Formats.-ipv6: Restricts IP logging output to IPv6 addresses.

Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-config: Path to the configuration file containing API access credentials and settings.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-dir: Directory where local persistent graph databases are generated or evaluated.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-dns-qps: Maximum outbound DNS queries per second.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-max-dns-queries: Legacy option for limiting parallel network lookups; described in the supplied notes as deprecated.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-r: Comma-separated custom DNS resolver IP addresses.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-rf: Path to a file containing custom DNS resolvers.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-tr: IP addresses of trusted resolvers used to identify wildcard DNS behavior.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-trf: Path to a file containing trusted resolver configurations.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-rqps: Peak query-per-second limit allocated to untrusted infrastructure.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-trqps: Query-per-second limit allocated to trusted infrastructure.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-timeout: Maximum total execution time in minutes before the scan ends.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-noresolvrate: Disables real-time monitoring of resolver performance constraints.
Concurrency, Networking & Timing.-noresolvscore: Disables logic used to score and rank resolver reliability.

MAN.About: dnsx is a fast and multi-purpose DNS toolkit used to resolve hosts and query DNS records.

Input.-l or -list: List of subdomains or hosts to resolve (file path, comma-separated values, or stdin).
Input.-d or -domain: List of target domains to brute-force (file path, comma-separated values, or stdin).
Input.-w or -wordlist: List of words to use for brute-forcing subdomains.

Query.-e or -exclude-type: Exclude specified DNS record types from queries.

Filter.-rc or -rcode: Filter results by DNS response codes.

Rate-Limit.-t: Control the number of concurrent threads.
Rate-Limit.-rl: Set the maximum number of requests per second.

Output.-o or -output: Save results to an output file.
Output.-omit-raw: Omit raw DNS response data from output.

Configuration & Optimization.-wd: Specify a domain for wildcard handling.
Configuration & Optimization.-auto-wildcard: Enable automatic wildcard detection and handling.

MAN.About: A fast and multi-purpose HTTP toolkit that allows running multiple probes using the retryablehttp library.

INPUT.-l, -list: Input file containing list of hosts to process

PROBES.-tech-detect: Display technology in use based on wappalyzer
PROBES.-websocket: Display if websocket connection is supported
PROBES.-cdn: Display target host CDN in use
PROBES.-probe: Display status code for successful probes

CONFIGURATIONS.-r, -resolvers: List of custom DNS resolvers to use
CONFIGURATIONS.-sni-name: Custom TLS SNI hostname to use
CONFIGURATIONS.-random-agent: Use a randomly selected User-Agent header
CONFIGURATIONS.-H, -header: Custom HTTP header to include in request
CONFIGURATIONS.-http-proxy: HTTP proxy to tunnel traffic through
CONFIGURATIONS.-unsafe: Send raw HTTP request skipping validation
CONFIGURATIONS.-max-redirects: Maximum number of redirects to follow
CONFIGURATIONS.-max-resp-size: Maximum response size to read in bytes

MATCHERS.-mc, -match-code: Match responses with specific status codes
MATCHERS.-ml, -match-length: Match responses with specific content lengths
MATCHERS.-mlc, -match-line-count: Match responses with specific line counts
MATCHERS.-mwc, -match-word-count: Match responses with specific word counts
MATCHERS.-mcdn, -match-cdn: Match responses from specific CDN providers

FILTERS.-fc, -filter-code: Filter out responses with specific status codes
FILTERS.-fl, -filter-length: Filter out responses with specific content lengths
FILTERS.-flc, -filter-line-count: Filter out responses with specific line counts
FILTERS.-fwc, -filter-word-count: Filter out responses with specific word counts
FILTERS.-fstring, -filter-string: Filter out responses containing specific string
FILTERS.-fregex, -filter-regex: Filter out responses matching specific regex
FILTERS.-fcdn, -filter-cdn: Filter out responses from specific CDN providers

RATE-LIMIT.-t, -threads: Number of concurrent threads to use
RATE-LIMIT.-rl, -rate-limit: Maximum number of requests to send per second
RATE-LIMIT.-rlm, -rate-limit-minute: Maximum number of requests to send per minute

OUTPUT.-sr, -store-response: Store raw HTTP responses in directory
OUTPUT.-json: Export output in JSON Lines format
OUTPUT.-include-chain: Include redirect chain in JSON output

OPTIMIZATION.-timeout: Timeout in seconds for network connections
OPTIMIZATION.-retry: Number of times to retry a failed request
OPTIMIZATION.-leave-default-ports: Retain default ports in output URLs

UPDATE.-up, -update: Update httpx binary to the latest version
UPDATE.-duc, -disable-update-check: Disable automatic update check on execution

DEBUG.-silent: Display only target results in output
DEBUG.-debug: Display full request and response debugging details

MAN.About: A high-performance directory/file, DNS, virtual host, and cloud bucket brute-forcing tool written in Go.

GLOBAL OPTIONS.-w, --wordlist: Path to the wordlist file used for brute-forcing
GLOBAL OPTIONS.-t, --threads: Number of concurrent threads to deploy (default: 10)
GLOBAL OPTIONS.--delay: Time interval each thread waits between requests
GLOBAL OPTIONS.-o, --output: Output file path to save discoveries (defaults to stdout)
GLOBAL OPTIONS.-q, --quiet: Silence the banner graphic and all non-essential notification noise
GLOBAL OPTIONS.-v, --verbose: Enable explicit logging outputs including connection errors
GLOBAL OPTIONS.--help, -h: Display contextual help layout guides for subcommands or core configuration

DIR MODE OPTIONS.-u, --url: Target web application base URL layout structure to bust
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-x, --extensions: File extensions to explicitly append to the wordlist parameters
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-s, --statuscodes: Comma-separated whitelist of positive status codes to match
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-b, --blackstatuscodes: Comma-separated blacklist of disruptive status codes to filter out
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-r, --followredirect: Instruct the processing logic to follow standard HTTP redirects
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-k, --insecure: Skip TLS certificate structure verification processes
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-e, --expanded: Print absolute long-form URLs instead of relative paths
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-c, --cookies: Custom cookies string data to send with outward web requests
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-H, --headers: Custom HTTP header blocks to inject into target traffic loads
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-a, --useragent: Override default HTTP User-Agent data strings
DIR MODE OPTIONS.--random-agent: Rotate and utilize random web client identifier signatures
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-m, --method: Specify alternative HTTP structural query method (e.g., POST, GET)
DIR MODE OPTIONS.--timeout: Maximum duration window allocation before network request exhaustion
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-U, --username: Username credentials required for Basic HTTP Access Authentication challenges
DIR MODE OPTIONS.-P, --password: Password credentials paired alongside the target Basic Auth profile username
DIR MODE OPTIONS.--exclude-length: Filter out responses sharing specific structural byte content sizes

DNS MODE OPTIONS.-d, --domain: Target apex structural base domain used for subdomain mapping actions
DNS MODE OPTIONS.-r, --resolver: Custom target structural upstream DNS server to issue requests to
DNS MODE OPTIONS.-c, --show-cname: Expose explicit underlying CNAME text pointer mappings
DNS MODE OPTIONS.-i, --show-ips: Expose explicitly resolved IPv4 or IPv6 records
DNS MODE OPTIONS.--wildcard: Force continuous query loops even after wildcard catches are found
DNS MODE OPTIONS.--timeout: Outbound DNS connection lifespan threshold limits before validation collapse

VHOST MODE OPTIONS.-u, --url: Target web infrastructure base IP layout map to point queries at
VHOST MODE OPTIONS.--append-domain: Append base target tracking apex domain elements directly onto elements parsed

CLOUD MODE OPTIONS (S3/GCS).-m, --maximpl: Maximum bucket instances validation concurrency rate structures
CLOUD MODE OPTIONS (S3/GCS).--provider: Direct service deployment engine tracking label target definition

MAN.About: A next-generation crawling and spidering framework designed to extract endpoints and metadata from web applications.

INPUT.-u, -list: Target URL or path to a file containing a list of target URLs to crawl
INPUT.-resume: Resume crawl session using a specified resume file

CONFIGURATION.-d, -depth: Maximum depth to follow links during crawling (default 3)
CONFIGURATION.-jc, -js-crawl: Enable JavaScript crawling and parsing mechanisms
CONFIGURATION.-jsl, -jsluice: Enable jsluice parsing for deeper JavaScript endpoint extraction
CONFIGURATION.-f, -form-parsing: Enable automated form parsing and extraction
CONFIGURATION.-r, -resolvers: List of custom DNS resolvers to use during operations
CONFIGURATION.-proxy: HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy URL to tunnel crawling traffic through
CONFIGURATION.-H, -header: Custom header or path to file containing custom headers to include in requests
CONFIGURATION.-b, -cookie: Custom cookies or path to file containing cookies to include in requests
CONFIGURATION.-ra, -random-agent: Use a randomly selected User-Agent header (default true)
CONFIGURATION.-inc, -include-mime: Comma-separated list of MIME types to explicitly include in crawl
CONFIGURATION.-exc, -exclude-mime: Comma-separated list of MIME types to explicitly exclude from crawl

SCOPE.-cs, -crawl-scope: In-scope URL regex or file containing regex patterns for crawling
SCOPE.-cos, -crawl-out-scope: Out-of-scope URL regex or file containing regex patterns to exclude
SCOPE.-field, -field-scope: Limit crawling scope to specific levels (e.g., 'rd' for root domain, 'fqdn' for subdomains)

FILTER.-mr, -match-regex: Match and display responses matching a specific regex pattern
FILTER.-fr, -filter-regex: Filter out and drop responses matching a specific regex pattern
FILTER.-e, -extension: Comma-separated list of file extensions to target or filter

RATE-LIMIT.-c, -concurrency: Number of concurrent concurrent targets to crawl (default 10)
RATE-LIMIT.-p, -parallelism: Number of parallel requests to process per target (default 10)
RATE-LIMIT.-rd, -rate-limit: Maximum number of HTTP requests to send per second
RATE-LIMIT.-rdm, -rate-limit-minute: Maximum number of HTTP requests to send per minute

OUTPUT.-o, -output: File path to write crawling results into
OUTPUT.-sr, -store-response: Store raw HTTP requests and responses in a dedicated directory
OUTPUT.-srd, -store-response-dir: Custom directory path to save stored raw responses
OUTPUT.-j, -jsonl: Export output in structured JSON Lines format
OUTPUT.-no-fields: Exclude extra metadata fields from standard text output

OPTIMIZATION.-timeout: Timeout duration in seconds for network connections (default 10)
OPTIMIZATION.-retry: Number of times to retry a failed HTTP request (default 1)
OPTIMIZATION.-sm, -strategy: Crawling approach strategy to apply (depth-first or breadth-first)

UPDATE.-up, -update: Update katana engine binary to the latest release version available
UPDATE.-duc, -disable-update-check: Disable automatic update check on application startup

DEBUG.-silent: Display only targeted output endpoints, silencing telemetry and banners
DEBUG.-v, -verbose: Enable verbose logging to track crawling progress and errors
DEBUG.-version: Display the active version details of Katana
DEBUG.-nc, -no-color: Disable ANSI color coding formatting inside terminal logs
